# Artifact Keeper 1.11.4

A maintenance release on the 1.11 line: 18 changelog entries from 17 pull requests since 1.11.3, all backported from `main`. The headline is **logout now revokes the session it ends** (#4831, GHSA-4x56-5942-m4fv): a bearer logout with an empty body and a web UI logout used to answer `200` while the session's refresh token kept minting access tokens. Next to it, **pushing a large OCI blob to an Azure-backed repository no longer fails with `500`** (#4858) once the copy that finalizes it runs past 30 seconds, with a new `AZURE_COPY_TIMEOUT_SECS` for slow accounts. Around them are three more security fixes (SAML response text decoding, plugin git fetches through the SSRF-guarded client, storage request URLs kept out of error messages), concurrent uploads to one path that now agree on a single winner and answer the losers `409` (#4832), an env-seeded LDAP provider that is disabled once `LDAP_*` is removed (#4857), storage fixes for repository delete, S3 and Azure, two NuGet V2 upstream fixes, and a Go 1.27.3 toolchain floor with a rebuilt bundled trivy. **No schema migrations.** One new setting, `AZURE_COPY_TIMEOUT_SECS`, which adds no floor when unset. Four security advisories for issues fixed in this release are published with it (see [Security](#security)).

## Read this first: what now answers with an error or refuses

- **Concurrent uploads to one artifact path agree on a single winner; the others get `409`** (#4832). An upload to a path that already holds a live artifact at the same version is refused with `409 CONFLICT` ("Artifact version already exists and is immutable") unless the repository has versioning enabled. That check ran before the bytes were stored and outside the transaction that writes the row, so several `PUT /api/v1/repositories/{key}/artifacts/{path}` requests racing to one free path could all pass it: each was answered `201`, and the last to commit silently replaced the content the others had been acknowledged for. The rule is now part of the row write itself, for direct uploads and for chunked-upload completion: exactly one racer gets `201` and keeps its bytes, and every other one gets the documented `409`. A client that fires parallel uploads of the same path and version, and treated every `201` as success, will now see `409` for all but one of them; a deleted artifact can still be replaced, and a versioning-enabled Generic or Mlmodel repository still appends a revision. The `409` is now in the OpenAPI description of the PUT.
- **SAML responses with a DOCTYPE or a non-predefined entity are refused** (#4827, GHSA-cp5x-hq47-4mg3). SAML responses are now read with entity references, character references and CDATA decoded, so the NameID, attributes and groups Artifact Keeper consumes are exactly the values the IdP signed. A Response that uses an entity other than the five predefined XML ones, or that carries a DOCTYPE, is refused, and whitespace inside a value is kept as signed instead of trimmed. Mainstream IdPs send neither; an IdP that does, or a value whose leading or trailing whitespace your group mappings relied on being trimmed, will need attention.

## Read this second: behaviour that changes without an error

- **Logout revokes the session's refresh token even when the refresh token is not in the request** (#4831, GHSA-4x56-5942-m4fv). `POST /api/v1/auth/logout` revoked the refresh-token family only when the request carried the refresh token, in the body or the `ak_refresh_token` cookie. A bearer logout with an empty body and a browser logout from the web UI carry neither. Access tokens minted with a refresh token now carry that session's family id, and logout revokes the presenting session's family whether or not the refresh token is included. Other sessions of the same user stay signed in, as before. Trade-off: access tokens issued before the upgrade carry no family id, so a logout presenting one of them behaves as before until that session next refreshes; sessions you need ended at once should log out with the refresh token, or be revoked by an administrator.
- **Azure Put Blob From URL copies are no longer cut off by the 30-second read timeout** (#4858). Every OCI blob finalize copies the uploaded bytes to their content-addressed key, and on Azure that copy is a synchronous Put Blob From URL for any source up to 5000 MiB. Azure answers only when the copy is done, but the request went out on the data-plane client, whose 30-second read timeout aborted it, so a blob of about 2 GiB failed with `500` "Azure Put Blob From URL failed: error sending request". Monolithic and chunked uploads, staged generic uploads (`/api/v1/uploads`) and proxy-cache staging-to-cache moves all end in this copy and are fixed together. The copy now has its own client with no read timeout and a per-request deadline of 60 seconds plus the source size at 8 MiB/s, and the source SAS outlives that deadline. Every other Azure request keeps the 30-second read timeout. **`AZURE_COPY_TIMEOUT_SECS`** sets a minimum for the copy deadline, in seconds, for accounts that copy slower than 8 MiB/s; unset, blank or non-numeric means no floor.
- **Removing the `LDAP_*` environment variables disables the LDAP provider they created** (#4857, #4863). A later boot without `LDAP_URL` / `LDAP_BASE_DN` used to leave the env-seeded provider enabled, so the login page kept offering only the LDAP form and local login stayed hidden for a directory the operator had removed. The boot now disables (never deletes) the provider the environment manages, as removing `OIDC_*` already does (#2819), and logs a warning naming it. Providers created through the admin API are never touched, and an administrator who re-enables the env-seeded provider through the admin API takes ownership of it, so later boots without `LDAP_*` leave it enabled. Trade-off: setting the `LDAP_*` variables again does **not** re-enable a provider the boot disabled; re-enable it through the admin API.
- **Members of the `repository-owner` role pass the repository `admin` check again** (#4818). Since 1.11.0 the repository administration routes (email subscriptions, the staging release target, upstream auth, egress proxy, routing rules, upstream filter, conda allowlist, PyPI tracks, the age gate and per-repository security settings) answered `403` to a `repository-owner` member, including the user who created the repository, because the check read fine-grained permission rules only. It now uses the same resolver as the write and delete checks, so a role carrying `admin` on the repository is honoured; `developer` and `reader` members are still refused.
- **The repository list and the repository update response report a Remote's upstream authentication** (#4851). `GET /api/v1/repositories` and `PATCH /api/v1/repositories/{key}` answered `upstream_auth_type: null` and `upstream_auth_configured: false` for every repository, while `GET /api/v1/repositories/{key}` reported them correctly; the web UI's edit dialog for a Remote reads the list row, so it showed no authentication configured. The list, create and update responses now set both fields as the detail response does. Only the auth type and whether one is configured are reported, never the credentials.
- **The migration jobs list's `pagination.total` honours the `status` filter** (#4800). `GET /api/v1/migrations?status=failed` narrowed the rows on the page but counted every job the caller could see, so `total_pages` and the UI's "N of M" were too large. Unfiltered totals are unchanged.
- **NuGet repositories translating a V2 upstream list the versions on every page of the upstream feed** (#4856). A Remote over a V2 OData feed, and a virtual repository merging a V2 member, read only the first page of `FindPackagesById()` and ignored the feed-level `<link rel="next">` continuation, so versions on later pages were missing and restores that needed one failed. The continuation is now followed, up to 20 pages per query, with rows repeated across pages listed once, and continuation pages are cached per URL next to the first page. A continuation must stay on the configured upstream origin (scheme, host and port), the only place the repository's upstream credentials are sent; one that points elsewhere is not requested, a warning is logged, and the pages already read are served. The raw V2 feed of a Remote was not affected.
- **NuGet V2 upstream translation keeps XML entities and the text before them** (#4816). Character and entity references (`&amp;`, `&#xF6;`) and CDATA sections in a V2 feed's description and authors overwrote the field instead of adding to it; the text is now accumulated across them.
- **Plugin git fetches go through the SSRF-guarded HTTP client** (#4827, GHSA-p28r-8m4q-w9pg). Plugin installs and reloads now connect only to an address the outbound policy admits at connect time, where libgit2 used to resolve the source host again after the URL check. Plugin git fetches also honour `HTTP_PROXY` / `HTTPS_PROXY` and `CUSTOM_CA_CERT_PATH` like the other outbound requests, so on a host with a proxy configured they now go through it.

## Read this third: operations and logging

- **Storage error messages carry the operation and the transport error, not the request URL** (#4866, GHSA-96xj-cjvj-hcg2). When a request to Azure Blob Storage failed in transport (connection reset, timeout), the error returned to the API client and written to the log repeated the full request URL, including its query string. They now name only the operation and the transport error. The network errors of a Google Cloud Storage resumable upload, which repeated the upload session URL, are trimmed the same way. Log searches that matched on the blob URL in these errors need to match on the operation instead.
- **Deleting a repository on filesystem storage removes its files even when another repository holds the same bytes** (#4833). The delete spared any content-addressed key another repository's row also named, but on filesystem storage each repository keeps its own copy under its own storage path, so the other copy wrongly shielded this one and, once the cascade dropped the rows, garbage collection could never find it. The check now counts only a repository that resolves the key to the same object (same backend, and on filesystem the same storage path). A key the delete still spares because it is genuinely shared is handed to the storage-GC candidate set, so the next GC pass reclaims it once no repository references it; that also covers two repositories sharing a key on cloud storage being deleted together. GC likewise reclaims a trashed filesystem copy while another repository serves its own copy. Space already orphaned by earlier deletes is not recovered by this change.
- **S3 storage reindex no longer reports artifacts with non-ASCII or reserved characters in their path as missing** (#4817). S3 listings, including the `S3_PROVIDER=oss` REST fallback, now return keys in the form reads and writes use, so `POST /api/v1/admin/repositories/{key}/reindex-storage` stops counting such an object as a missing row plus an unregistered ghost, and proxy-cache purges and RPM version retention can delete it. Existing object keys are not rewritten. An object written by another tool under a key Artifact Keeper can neither read nor write (for example a raw `~`) is left out of the listing with a warning.
- **Server-side S3 copy of a large object with a non-ASCII or reserved character in its path no longer fails with `NoSuchKey`** (#4838). The multipart `UploadPartCopy` path, which every object above `S3_MAX_SINGLE_COPY_BYTES` takes, encoded the caller's key instead of the stored one in `x-amz-copy-source`; it now sends the URL encoding of the stored key, as the single-request `CopyObject` already did.

## Dependency and image updates

- **Go toolchain floor go1.27.3 for every Go binary, and the scanner adapter's bundled trivy rebuilt on it, published as scanner adapter 1.5.1** (#4852). This clears CVE-2026-111943 (HIGH, Go stdlib). `GO_MIN_PATCH` moves from 1.27.2 to 1.27.3 in the backend, Alpine backend and scanner adapter Dockerfiles at once, since the stdlib is a property of the compiler rather than of the image that was reported, and a new `scripts/ci/check-go-floor-agreement.sh` fails any PR that leaves the floors disagreeing. The bundled trivy moves from `ghcr.io/artifact-keeper/trivy:0.76.0-r1` to `0.76.0-r2`, the same upstream Trivy v0.76.0 rebuilt on go1.27.3; the trivy release is unchanged, so a self-run trivy server stays on 0.76.0. The adapter is 1.5.1 on this line (1.6.0 is the 1.12.0 line's adapter tag).
- **wasmtime 36.0.19** for the WASM plugin runtime (#4842; RUSTSEC-2026-0379, RUSTSEC-2026-0380): two Cranelift code-generation defects in 36.0.18 could miscompile plugin code. `wasmtime` and `wasmtime-wasi` move together; no configuration change.
- **rustls-webpki 0.103.16 and webpki-roots / webpki-root-certs 1.0.10** (#4861; RUSTSEC-2026-0381, RUSTSEC-2026-0382, RUSTSEC-2026-0383): the previous versions could accept a chain through a distrusted intermediate, and the bundled roots still trusted the distrusted emSign intermediates. No configuration change.

## Security

Four GitHub security advisories cover issues fixed in 1.11.4 and will be published with this release. Upgrading to 1.11.4 covers all four.

- [GHSA-cp5x-hq47-4mg3](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/security/advisories/GHSA-cp5x-hq47-4mg3) (High): SAML assertion text loses XML entity and character references, so different IdP identities map to one AK account (#4827).
- [GHSA-4x56-5942-m4fv](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/security/advisories/GHSA-4x56-5942-m4fv) (Medium): Logout does not revoke the session's refresh token when the refresh token is not included in the logout request (#4831).
- [GHSA-96xj-cjvj-hcg2](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/security/advisories/GHSA-96xj-cjvj-hcg2) (Medium): Azure storage errors expose a write-capable SAS URL to the client (#4866).
- [GHSA-p28r-8m4q-w9pg](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/security/advisories/GHSA-p28r-8m4q-w9pg) (Low): Plugin reload: hostname re-resolved by libgit2 after SSRF validation (DNS rebinding window) (#4827).

The dependency and image updates above also clear CVE-2026-111943 and RUSTSEC-2026-0379, 0380, 0381, 0382 and 0383.

The full entries are in the `## [1.11.4]` section of [CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/artifact-keeper/artifact-keeper/blob/v1.11.4/CHANGELOG.md).
